metadata.title: Beer brands commonly encountered around Iberia
metadata.method: Hand-compiled orientation guide, not exclusivity, draught availability or a live sales ranking. Markers favour a locally meaningful or especially characteristic brand; popups name the other common national and distributor brands.
metadata.logo_note: Brand marks are used for identification and remain the property of their respective owners.

logo_sources.super-bock: Super Bock brand mark via Wikimedia Commons
logo_sources.especial: Melo Abreu label image via Pint Please; regional identity verified by Marca Açores

markets.status: The home-region brewery from A Coruña and the clearest default to recognise.
markets.also: 1906, Mahou, local craft beer.
markets.note: Despite its national reach, Hijos de Rivera remains family-owned, based in Galicia and independent, with 100% Spanish capital.

markets.status: A very common national tap in Asturias, where cider—not beer—carries the local identity.
markets.also: Estrella Galicia; Franziskaner, Spaten, Löwenbräu and Beck's through Mahou's AB InBev relationship.
markets.note: The twist: Damm's Font Salem operation makes supermarket-label beer in Meres, Asturias, while Mahou's distribution deal puts this conspicuously Munich-looking shelf into local bars.

markets.status: A common hospitality tap across Cantabria.
markets.also: Mahou, Estrella Galicia and local craft breweries.
markets.note: Amstel and southern-looking Cruzcampo are both Heineken España brands: regional tap maps often reveal hospitality portfolios as much as local taste.

markets.status: The most explicitly Basque legacy lager to recognise, especially around Gipuzkoa.
markets.also: San Miguel, Mahou, Heineken and a strong craft scene.
markets.note: Keler's identity is Basque, but it belongs to Damm; Damm's 2020 reporting lists it among the brands produced and packaged at El Prat de Llobregat.

markets.status: A familiar northern Spanish bar and restaurant beer.
markets.also: Ambar, Mahou and local craft beer.
markets.note: Pacharán and wine are more distinctively Navarrese than any mass lager.

markets.status: The neighbouring Aragón brewery is easy to encounter in Logroño and the Ebro valley.
markets.also: Mahou and Estrella Galicia.
markets.note: Wine is the regional identity; beer here is the bar-ordering map.

markets.status: Zaragoza's historic brewery and Aragón's unmistakable regional label.
markets.also: Mahou and San Miguel.
markets.note: Unlike most big regional labels on this map, Ambar still describes itself as an independent brewer.

markets.status: The capital's home lager and the default caña in a great many Madrid bars.
markets.also: Every national brand, plus a large craft scene.
markets.note: Ask only for una caña and Mahou is a likely answer.

markets.status: The most broadly encountered national tap across the region.
markets.also: Estrella Galicia, Ambar and local craft beer.
markets.note: The region is too large for a single brewery culture; this is practical orientation.

markets.status: Madrid's brewery has strong reach across central Spain.
markets.also: Estrella Galicia, Amstel and local craft beer.
markets.note: Wine is local; the familiar lager tap is generally national.

markets.status: A common national bar beer across Extremadura.
markets.also: Cruzcampo in the south, Estrella Galicia and local craft beer.
markets.note: A distribution-led answer in a region without one dominant mass-market identity brand.

markets.status: Barcelona's home lager and the regional brand visitors see everywhere.
markets.also: Moritz, Voll-Damm and a deep craft scene.
markets.note: Estrella on its own usually means Damm here; in Galicia it means something else.

markets.status: The revived Valencia-born toasted lager is the most characterful local label to spot.
markets.also: Amstel, Estrella de Levante and Mahou.
markets.note: Turia is Valencia-born, but it belongs to Damm; Damm's 2020 reporting places its production and packaging at El Prat de Llobregat.

markets.status: The Catalan brewery has a very visible hospitality presence across the islands.
markets.also: Rosa Blanca in Mallorca, San Miguel and imported resort beers.
markets.note: Mallorca's revived Rosa Blanca is another Damm label that its 2020 reporting places in the El Prat production network; resort contracts decide which cousin reaches the tap.

markets.status: Seville's brewery and the dominant visual language of western Andalusian beer terraces.
markets.also: Victoria from Málaga, national brands and Radler-style shandies.
markets.note: Cruzcampo belongs to Heineken España; Granada's rival Alhambra has belonged to Mahou San Miguel since 2007. The regional divide is also a contest between portfolios.

markets.status: Granada's home beer, especially visible in the east and in tapas bars.
markets.also: Cruzcampo, Victoria and national brands.
markets.note: Alhambra still brews in Granada, but it has belonged to Madrid's Mahou San Miguel since 2007: local identity and corporate ownership point in different directions.

markets.status: Brewed outside Murcia city and tightly associated with the region.
markets.also: Mahou, Amstel and Alhambra.
markets.note: It belongs to Damm, but unlike Damm's revived Keler and Turia identities it is still brewed in its home region, at the Murcia factory.

markets.status: The southern mainland distribution pattern carries across the strait.
markets.also: San Miguel, Mahou and alcohol-free beer.
markets.note: Availability varies sharply between Spanish bars and Muslim-owned cafés.

markets.status: A familiar Spanish hospitality brand in the city.
markets.also: Mahou, Cruzcampo and alcohol-free beer.
markets.note: As in Ceuta, neighbourhood and venue type matter more than a single city allegiance.

markets.area: Gran Canaria and the eastern islands
markets.status: Gran Canaria's historic local lager—the one with the dog—and the characteristic eastern-island label.
markets.also: Dorada, imported brands and Tropical 1924.
markets.note: Tropical and Tenerife's Dorada have been in the same Compañía Cervecera de Canarias since a 1994 merger; that company became part of AB InBev in 2016. The fierce island distinction survives inside one multinational.

markets.status: Tenerife's home lager and the characteristic western-island label.
markets.also: Tropical, imported brands and Dorada Especial.
markets.note: Dorada and Gran Canaria's Tropical are market rivals but corporate siblings; their AB InBev-owned brewer also distributes Beck's, Leffe and Franziskaner in the islands.

markets.status: Born near Porto and the default northern Portuguese beer identity.
markets.also: Sagres and a growing craft scene.
markets.note: Portugal's north–south duel is not purely local: Super Bock Group is 44% Carlsberg, while Sagres's producer has belonged to Heineken since 2008.

markets.status: Common across the north and centre, with especially strong recognition from Porto southwards.
markets.also: Sagres and local craft beer.
markets.note: This is the overlap zone between Portugal's two national giants.

markets.status: One of the two ubiquitous Portuguese lagers, used here as the more useful central marker.
markets.also: Sagres everywhere; craft beer around the larger towns.
markets.note: Expect both national brands rather than a clean regional monopoly.

markets.status: Lisbon's home-side national brand and a likely imperial on the capital's terraces.
markets.also: Super Bock and a large craft scene.
markets.note: Sagres remains brewed at Vialonga near Lisbon, but its producer has been part of Heineken since 2008. Ask for an imperial and that distribution network often chooses the brand.

markets.status: The Lisbon-and-south national brand is commonly encountered around Setúbal.
markets.also: Super Bock and local craft beer.
markets.note: Moscatel, not lager, is the genuinely local bottle.

markets.status: The more characteristic national lager across Lisbon and southern Portugal.
markets.also: Super Bock and small regional breweries.
markets.note: The region's identity drink is wine; this marker answers what is likely behind the bar.

markets.status: The familiar Portuguese resort and restaurant tap across the south.
markets.also: Super Bock plus British, Irish and German imports in resort areas.
markets.note: Imported draught lines often reflect tourism and supply contracts more than Algarvian taste.

markets.status: Melo Abreu's São Miguel-brewed local lager.
markets.also: Super Bock, Sagres and Especial Melo Abreu variants.
markets.note: A genuinely archipelago-made beer rather than a mainland distribution answer.

markets.status: Madeira's local lager, brewed by Empresa de Cervejas da Madeira.
markets.also: Super Bock, Sagres and imported resort brands.
markets.note: Coral is the island identity; poncha is the more distinctive drink.
